dati_metodo: US VC firms and VC-backed portfolio companies, investments 1975-2005, firm locations from Pratt's Guide; localization measures (C(3), location quotient, spatial Gini), OLS regressions on office location and on investment success by VC-center status and distance/locality.

righe.estrazione: Contradicts the tesi: the paper shows that VC firms and VC-backed companies are geographically concentrated (three metro areas hold over half of VC offices and 49% of US VC-backed companies), but it also finds that most investments (57%) are made by VC firms outside their home CSA. It does not estimate how the probability or volume of investment falls with distance; distance enters only in analysing success/outperformance, where non-local investments outperform local ones. A narrower point the txt does support: VC firms and VC-backed companies are highly clustered geographically.
righe.citazione: Overall, most investments (57%) are made by venture capital firms outside of their home CSA.
righe.posizione: 5. Geography of venture capital-backed portfolio companies
righe.numero_chiave: 57%: share of investments made by VC firms outside their home CSA; 49%: share of US VC-backed companies located in San Francisco, Boston and New York
righe.limiti_vs_noi: Investments 1975-2005, not 2012-2019; the unit is VC firm office location and outperformance by distance, not round timing or exit within five years.
righe.note: Compound tesi: 'is local' is contradicted by the 57% non-local share (though concentration of VC is shown); 'falls with distance' is not shown for investment. Shared with sorenson2001; judged only on this txt. If the group wants to keep the citation, narrow the tesi to geographic clustering of VC firms and companies.
